teachingContexts.title: Further Transformations: absolute-value graph transformations

methods.statement: For y=|f(x)|, retain points on or above the x-axis and reflect points below it in the x-axis. The domain and x-intercepts remain unchanged.

For y=f(|x|), retain the original nonnegative-x portion, discard the negative-x portion and reflect a copy of the retained portion in the y-axis. The resulting domain consists of x for which |x| belongs to the original domain.

Use fixed intercepts and reflected key points to construct the transformed sketch. Output absolute value preserves every zero; input absolute value reflects the nonnegative-x zeros into symmetric pairs.
Transform supplied graphical paths directly without assigning unsupported equations or exact turning-point coordinates. Reflect the relevant Bézier endpoints and control points consistently.

teachingContexts.title: Further Transformations — teaching context

methods.statement: Form the reciprocal only where f is defined and nonzero. Map (a,b) to (a,1/b), preserve signs, and retain points with ordinate 1 or -1.
Locate reciprocal vertical asymptotes using one-sided approaches of f to zero. Determine each branch's infinite direction from the sign of f.

Determine reciprocal end behaviour from the limiting ordinates of f: positive or negative infinity gives approach to zero from the corresponding side; a nonzero horizontal limit c gives horizontal limit 1/c.

Reciprocate nonzero turning-point ordinates and interchange maxima and minima where f stays on one side of the x-axis locally. Reverse increasing and decreasing behaviour separately on intervals of constant nonzero sign.

Construct reciprocal sketches by combining excluded zeros, asymptotes, one-sided limits, mapped intercepts and turning points, symmetry and monotonicity. Use graphical information without requiring an invented equation or exact coordinates for unlabelled features.
For y=|f(x)|, retain the portions on or above the x-axis and reflect negative portions in the x-axis. Preserve the original domain and zeros; the supplied crossing zeros become sharp minima.

For y=f(|x|), retain the nonnegative-x portion, remove the original negative-x portion and reflect a copy of the retained portion in the y-axis. The domain consists of x-values for which |x| belongs to the original domain.

teachingContexts.title: Further Transformations — reciprocal-function teaching context

methods.statement: Restrict the reciprocal to points where the original function is defined and nonzero. Map (a,b) to (a,1/b), preserving the abscissa and sign; points with ordinate ±1 remain fixed.
Locate vertical asymptotes using one-sided approaches of the original ordinate to zero from above or below. Determine the reciprocal's corresponding positive or negative infinite behaviour.
Determine end behaviour by reciprocating limits: original ordinates tending to ±∞ produce reciprocal ordinates tending to zero with the same sign. A nonzero horizontal asymptote y=c becomes y=1/c.
Reciprocate nonzero turning-point ordinates while retaining their abscissae. Where the function remains on one side of the x-axis nearby, maxima become minima and minima become maxima.
Reverse increasing and decreasing behaviour separately on intervals where the original function remains strictly positive or strictly negative.

Construct reciprocal sketches from asymptotes, one-sided behaviour, mapped points, turning points and monotonicity. Calculate the y-intercept when the original function is defined and nonzero at x=0; the reciprocal has no x-intercepts.

Use graphical information directly when an equation is not supplied. Preserve noninteger zero positions and graphical turning-point information without requiring invented exact equations or coordinates.

issues.statement: The rule asserts a vertical asymptote whenever f(x) approaches zero from one side, without specifying a signed, nonzero approach. An unsigned zero limit alone does not guarantee that the reciprocal tends to either +∞ or −∞; the function could alternate sign or be zero throughout that side.
issues.proposedRepair: Replace the sentence with: 'Where f(x) approaches 0 from above or below as x approaches a from at least one side, using values where f(x) is defined and nonzero, draw the vertical asymptote x=a.' This aligns the rule with p4-key-ideas-zero and the following signed-limit statements.

teachingContexts.title: Further Transformations: adding and subtracting graphs

methods.statement: Form sums by adding ordinates at the same x-coordinate, only where both functions are defined. Algebraic addition is permitted when equations are given, but ordinate addition is the taught focus.
Form differences by subtracting the g ordinate from the f ordinate at the same x-coordinate, retaining the sign of each ordinate.
Plot representative ordinate sums or differences, then connect them with the appropriate continuous curve or straight branches. Preserve corners and included joining points.
For reciprocal components, exclude x=0, keep branches disconnected, determine one-sided behaviour near the vertical asymptote, and infer outer-tail behaviour from the component ordinates.
